Hi Sam —

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps: 

- What we covered: Hosted API quickstart, sample endpoint calls, streaming demo, basic rate limit behavior.
- Your stated priorities: fast time-to-value for customer support use case, predictable latency (<200ms p50 for 512 tokens), and a simple procurement path.
- Outstanding questions from your side: per-client rate limits, burst capacity, and SSO/procurement timeline.

Next steps I suggest:
1) I’ll share our Hosted API quickstart doc and a small sandbox key so your engineers can run a smoke test (low effort).
2) We’ll schedule a short follow-up with Logan (solutions engineer) to walk through integration patterns and rate-limit headers.
3) If the sandbox looks good, we can propose pricing for hosted vs. dedicated capacity (I’ll attach the high-level ratecard).

I attached the quickstart guide and the Q4 ratecard for reference.

Availability: I can do 30 minutes on Wednesday 12/2 or Thursday 12/3 in the morning PT — does either work?

Thanks — Marissa

Great, thanks Sam — confirming Wed 12/2 09:30 PT. I’ve provisioned a sandbox API key and included instructions below for a quick smoke test (also attached as PDF).

Sandbox quickstart (curl):
1) Endpoint: https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
2) Header: Authorization: Bearer sandbox-xxxxxx
3) Example body: {"model":"redwood-1-small","input":"Summarize this support ticket: ...","max_tokens":256}

Rate limits and quotas (hosted):
- Default account-level burst: 300 r/s (short bursts; sustained above this triggers throttling)
- Default sustained: 60 r/s per account (we can configure per-key overrides for pilots)
- Per-key limits: supported via our API keys & usage policies — Logan will propose a per-key policy matching your 50 r/s sustained with a 250 r/s burst window.
- Rate-limit headers returned: X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset

Logan, can you confirm the implementation pattern for per-key overrides and the timeline to enable a custom policy for Acme?

Procurement questions: Aditya — looping you in for SOC 2 evidence and typical contract cadence for hosted pilots. Sam, procurement can expect our SOC 2 report and standard DPA; we typically handle pilot agreements on a short MSA + SOW.

Attachments: redwood-hosted-quickstart.pdf, redwood-ratecard-q4-2026.xlsx

See you Wed.

Best,
Marissa

--

Hi all —

Quick technical note ahead of Wednesday’s call:
- We can implement per-key sustained and burst limits via our API gateway policies. For your stated requirements (50 r/s sustained, 250 r/s burst), we estimate a small config change that can be turned on within 1 business day once the pilot account is provisioned.
- Observability: logs and token-level cost breakdown are available in the Console for the sandbox; we’ll enable a dedicated view for Acme.
- If you need lower latency SLOs or dedicated throughput, we can map out Dedicated capacity options (reserved GPU pools) on the follow-up call. For now, Hosted should meet your needs for an initial pilot.

I’ll prepare a short runbook for Wednesday with curl examples and expected headers.
